definition_en: a small wheel with a grooved rim around which a rope or belt runs, used to lift or pull loads
core_image: 一只带凹槽的小轮子，绳子绕过它，轻手一拉重物就升起
scene: 工人在仓库的横梁上装了一个滑轮，一个人就拉动了两大桶水。A worker fixed a pulley to the beam of the warehouse, and one man alone hauled two heavy buckets of water.
sceneCN: 这里 pulley 是「滑轮」（第 1 个义项：绕绳提升重物的小轮）；句意：工人在仓库的横梁上装了一个滑轮，一个人就拉动了两大桶水。

pos.zh: 滑轮；滑车
用滑轮提升（较少见）

derivatives.zh: 滑轮组：滑轮装在同一个框架里，连成可以成倍省力的装置
滑轮轮体：复合词，指带凹槽、绕绳的那个轮子本身

senses.title: A grooved wheel for lifting loads
senses.definition: a wheel with a groove around its edge, over which a rope or belt runs to lift or pull a heavy load
senses.definitionCN: 边缘带凹槽、绳索或皮带绕其转动的轮子，用来提升或拉动重物
senses.example: They raised the timber with a rope and a single pulley.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一根绳子和一个滑轮把木料吊了上去。
senses.why: The core image is a wheel that changes the direction of a pull, so the simple machine is the oldest and most central sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个改变拉力方向的小轮子，所以这种简单机械是最古老也最核心的义项。

senses.title: A block and pulley system
senses.definition: a frame holding one or more wheels of this kind, forming a lifting device
senses.definitionCN: 装有一个或多个此类轮子的框架，构成升降装置
senses.example: The crane uses a heavy pulley block to raise steel beams.
senses.exampleCN: 起重机用沉重的滑轮组吊起钢梁。
senses.why: When several such wheels are fixed in one frame, the name shifts from the wheel to the whole lifting device.
senses.whyCN: 当几个这样的轮子固定在一个框架里时，名称就从单个轮子扩展到整个起重装置。

senses.title: A wheel in a belt drive
senses.definition: a wheel in a machine over which a belt passes to transmit power
senses.definitionCN: 机器中供皮带绕过、用来传递动力的轮子
senses.example: A worn pulley made the drive belt slip badly.
senses.exampleCN: 一个磨损的皮带轮使传动皮带严重打滑。
senses.why: The same grooved wheel works in reverse: instead of lifting a load, it carries motion from one shaft to another.
senses.whyCN: 同一种带槽的轮子可以反向工作：它不吊起货物，而是把运动从一根轴传到另一根轴。

senses.title: To raise with a pulley
senses.definition: to hoist or move something with the help of a pulley
senses.definitionCN: 借助滑轮把某物吊起或移动
senses.example: They pulleyed the engine onto the deck of the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用滑轮把发动机吊到船甲板上。
senses.why: Informal technical use turns the noun into a verb, naming the action that the device performs.
senses.whyCN: 技术圈的非正式用法把名词动词化，用来描述这种装置所执行的动作。

intro.en: Pulley comes through Anglo-French polie from a Latin or Greek word for a small pulley or ball.
intro.cn: pulley 经由盎格鲁-法语 polie 传入，源头一般认为来自拉丁语或希腊语中表示小滑轮、圆球的词。

items.en: Greek polos means a turning axis or a round ball.
items.cn: 希腊语 polos 意为转轴或圆球。

items.en: Latin polleys records a small pulley used with ropes.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 polleys 记录了一种配绳使用的小滑轮。

items.en: The form polie enters English through Anglo-French.
items.cn: 形式 polie 经由盎格鲁-法语进入英语。

items.en: Pulley is first recorded in Middle English writing on building work.
items.cn: pulley 最早见于中古英语的建筑工程文字。

items.en: The word names both lifting blocks and belt wheels in machinery.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词既指起重滑车，也指机械里的皮带轮。

note.en: Pulley is a rope-and-wheel word, close to pulley block and to other simple machine words.
note.cn: pulley 是「绳与轮」的词，与滑轮组以及其它简单机械词相邻。

entries.definition: to move something towards you or after you
entries.definitionCN: 拉；拖（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a young hen
entries.definitionCN: 小母鸡（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: an uncommon older spelling of pulley
entries.definitionCN: pulley 较少见的旧式拼写（同源异拼）

entries.definition: a machine with a turning drum for pulling in a rope
entries.definitionCN: 绞车；用转筒收绳的机械

entries.definition: an apparatus for lifting heavy objects
entries.definitionCN: 起重机；升降装置

entries.definition: the grooved wheel inside a pulley block
entries.definitionCN: 滑轮里的带槽轮体

normalIntro.en: Pulley is a small wheel in a groove, and the name came from Latin and French for a round turning part.
normalIntro.cn: pulley 是嵌在槽里的小轮子，名字来自拉丁语和法语中表示圆形转动部件的词。

normal.en: A pulley is a wheel with a groove, and a rope runs in the groove.
normal.cn: pulley 是带凹槽的轮子，绳子就在凹槽里滑动。

normal.en: A pulley block holds several wheels in one frame.
normal.cn: pulley block 在一个框架里装好几个轮子。

normal.en: Pair pulley with belt when the wheel drives machinery.
normal.cn: 当轮子用来驱动机器时，常与 belt 搭配成皮带传动。

normal.en: A sheave is only the wheel, while a pulley includes its frame and rope.
normal.cn: sheave 只是轮体，而 pulley 还包括框架和绳子。

normal.en: Compare winch: a winch winds the rope, a pulley redirects it.
normal.cn: 对比 winch：绞车把绳子卷起来，滑轮则改变绳子的方向。

abstract.en: Picture a rope sliding over a smooth wheel and a bucket rising.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子在光滑的轮子上滑动，水桶随之上升。

abstract.en: Picture three wheels stacked in a frame as a lifting team.
abstract.cn: 想象三个轮子装进一个框架里，像一个起重小队。

abstract.en: Picture a belt running over a wheel inside a factory machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一条皮带在工厂机器里的轮子上转动。

examples.en: The sailors used a rope and pulley to hoist the heavy anchor.
examples.cn: 水手们用绳子和滑轮把沉重的锚吊起来。

examples.en: Criminals blocked the pulley of the old elevator with a wooden beam.
examples.cn: 有人用一根木梁卡住了旧电梯的滑轮。

examples.en: The engineer replaced the worn pulley in the conveyor system.
examples.cn: 工程师更换了传送系统里磨损的皮带轮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑利」——小轮子一扑一顿地把重物往上「利索」地拉起；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 polos（转轴、圆球）→ 中世纪拉丁语 polleys（小滑轮）→ 盎格鲁-法语 polie → 中古英语 pulley，核心义「绕绳的小轮」。词源链条中间环节存在不同说法，此处采用常见的一家。

sensesIntro.en: Pulley starts from the single grooved wheel, widens to a block of wheels, then to a belt wheel, and finally becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: pulley 从单个带槽的轮子出发，扩展为多轮组成的滑车，再指皮带轮，最后动词化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small grooved wheel that a rope runs over.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带槽的小轮子，绳子从上面滑过。

branches.en: The single grooved wheel is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 单个带槽的轮子是最基本的义项。

branches.en: A frame of wheels forms the lifting block.
branches.cn: 多个轮子装进框架就构成滑车组。

branches.en: A wheel under a belt transmits power.
branches.cn: 皮带下的轮子用来传递动力。

branches.en: Both the wheel and the block gain force by guiding the rope.
branches.cn: 单个轮子和滑车组都靠引导绳子来省力。

branches.en: The verb simply names the action of hoisting with the device.
branches.cn: 动词义不过是用这种装置吊起的动作。

intro.en: Pulley is borrowed whole, and English builds compounds and related nouns around it.
intro.cn: pulley 是整体借入的词，英语围绕它构成复合词和相关名词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin polleys and Greek polos underlie the round turning part.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 polleys 与希腊语 polos 构成「圆形转动部件」这一意思。

items.meaning: a turning axis or round ball
items.example: Polos gives the round turning idea.
items.exampleCN: polos 提供「圆形转动」的意象。

items.example: Polleys names the rope wheel in building texts.
items.exampleCN: polleys 在建筑文字中指点绳索用的轮子。

items.example: Pulley is the modern noun.
items.exampleCN: pulley 是现代名词。

items.example: Pulleys often works in a set.
items.exampleCN: 滑轮常常成组使用。

items.example: Pulley block names the whole lifting frame.
items.exampleCN: pulley block 指整个起重框架。

items.example: Sheave is the inner wheel.
items.exampleCN: sheave 指内部的轮体。

items.example: Winch winds the rope instead of turning it.
items.exampleCN: 绞车把绳子卷起，而不是改变其方向。

items.example: Hoist describes the lifting action.
items.exampleCN: hoist 描述吊起的动作。

definition_zh: 磨碎；粉碎；彻底击败；抨击
definition_en: to crush something into small pieces or powder, or to defeat or criticize someone completely
core_image: 一整块石头被木槌敲到只剩一层细尘
scene: 药剂师把干草药放进研钵，用力研磨，直到剩下细细的粉末。The chemist placed the dried herbs in a mortar and pulverise it until only fine powder was left.
sceneCN: 这里 pulverise 是「磨碎、粉碎」（第 1 个义项：把固体研磨成粉末）；句意：药剂师把干草药放进研钵，用力研磨，直到剩下细细的粉末。

pos.zh: 磨碎；粉碎
彻底击败；猛烈抨击（比喻）
被磨成粉；碎裂

derivatives.zh: pulverise + -ation 构成的抽象名词，义为「粉碎；研磨；彻底击溃」
pulverise + -er 构成的施动名词，指「粉碎机；研磨者」
过去分词作形容词，义为「被粉碎的；磨成粉的」
与 pulvis 同源的形容义词，义为「粉状的；覆满灰尘的」

senses.title: To grind something into powder
senses.definition: to crush or grind a solid into fine particles or powder
senses.definitionCN: 把固体碾碎或研磨成细小颗粒或粉末
senses.example: The mill pulverises limestone into powder for cement.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把石灰石粉碎成水泥用的粉末。
senses.why: The Latin source means dust, so the first sense is simply to turn something into dust.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词源本义就是「灰尘」，所以第一个义项就是把某物变成灰尘。

senses.title: To destroy something completely
senses.definition: to break something into very small pieces, or to damage it beyond repair
senses.definitionCN: 把某物击成碎片，或损坏到无法修复
senses.example: The explosion pulverised the concrete wall.
senses.exampleCN: 爆炸把混凝土墙炸得粉碎。
senses.why: Physical smashing extends from grinding to any force that leaves only rubble behind.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的砸碎从研磨延伸到任何只留下碎屑的破坏力量。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent decisively
senses.definition: to beat a rival or team completely in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中把对手或对手球队彻底打败
senses.example: The champions pulverised their rivals in the final set.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军们在最后一盘彻底击溃了对手。
senses.why: When an opponent is crushed like rock, the sports headline borrows the same dust image.
senses.whyCN: 当对手像石头一样被碾碎时，体育报道借用了同一幅「成尘」的画面。

senses.title: To attack an idea or person severely
senses.definition: to criticise an argument, person, or policy very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 对论点、某人或政策加以极其严厉的批评
senses.example: The reviewer pulverised the novel in a single paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家用一段话就把这部小说批得体无完肤。
senses.why: Words can grind an argument to dust just as a hammer grinds stone, giving the figurative critical sense.
senses.whyCN: 言语能像锤子砸石头一样把论点碾成粉末，由此产生比喻性的批评义。

senses.title: To break down into tiny pieces
senses.definition: to fall or crumble into fine fragments, often of rock or soil
senses.definitionCN: 碎裂成细小碎块，常用于岩石或土壤
senses.example: The dry cliffs pulverise under the constant wind.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的崖壁在不停的风中碎成粉屑。
senses.why: The intransitive use keeps the same image but makes the material the subject that crumbles.
senses.whyCN: 不作及物用法时保留同一意象，只是把碎裂的材料变成句子的主体。

intro.en: Pulverise goes back to Latin pulvis, dust, through the verb pulverizare and French pulveriser.
intro.cn: pulverise 源出拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘），经动词 pulverizare 与法语 pulveriser 进入英语。

items.en: Pulvis means dust that settles after grinding.
items.cn: pulvis 意为研磨后落下的灰尘。

items.en: Pulverizare means to reduce to dust.
items.cn: pulverizare 意为使化为灰尘。

items.en: Pulverise first appears in English after the French form.
items.cn: pulverise 随法语形式在英语中后期首次出现。

items.en: The verb spreads from chemistry to geology and journalism.
items.cn: 这个动词从化学扩展到地质学与新闻评论。

items.en: American spelling often writes it with -ize.
items.cn: 二十世纪起，美式拼写常写作 -ize 形式。

note.en: Pulverise is the dust verb of Latin pulvis, close to pulverisation and to other crushing words.
note.cn: pulverise 是拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘）衍生出的动词，与 pulverisation 及其它「碾碎」词相邻。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写（同源异拼）

entries.definition: the act of grinding something to powder
entries.definitionCN: 粉碎；研磨（同根派生名词）

entries.definition: the Latin word for dust
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的「灰尘」

entries.definition: to crush something into very small pieces
entries.definitionCN: 磨碎；磨成粉

entries.definition: to press something until it breaks
entries.definitionCN: 压碎；压扁

entries.definition: to destroy a building completely
entries.definitionCN: 拆毁；彻底破坏

normalIntro.en: Pulverise is built from Latin pulvis, dust, so the word always points to something being reduced to dust.
normalIntro.cn: pulverise 由拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘）构成，因此这个词总指向「化为灰尘」。

normal.en: The root pulver- is the same dust root found in pulverised powder.
normal.cn: 词根 pulver- 就是「灰尘」的词根，与 pulverised powder 中的部分同源。

normal.en: The suffix -ise forms a verb of making, so pulverise means to make dust.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ise 构成「使……化」的动词，所以 pulverise 就是使某物变成灰。

normal.en: Pulverised limestone is a common collocation in factory reports.
normal.cn: pulverised limestone 是工厂报告里常见的搭配。

normal.en: The noun is pulverisation, formed with the abstract suffix -ation.
normal.cn: 名词是 pulverisation，由抽象后缀 -ation 构成。

normal.en: American texts spell the word pulverize with a z.
normal.cn: 美式文本把它拼作 pulverize，用 z 代替 s。

abstract.en: Picture a pestle striking dried herbs until a cloud of dust rises.
abstract.cn: 想象杵反复敲击干草药，直到扬起一团尘雾。

abstract.en: Picture a wall dissolving into rubble after a blast.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙在爆炸后化成满地碎块。

abstract.en: Picture a team so beaten that its game plan lies in pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一支球队被打得溃不成军，作战计划也碎成片。

examples.en: Volcanic eruptions pulverise rock into fine ash.
examples.cn: 火山喷发把岩石粉碎成细灰。

examples.en: The home team was pulverised by three quick goals.
examples.cn: 主队被三个快攻进球彻底打垮。

examples.en: She pulverised every weak point in the proposal with one sharp question.
examples.cn: 她用一个尖锐的问题就把提案里所有薄弱之处驳倒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扒我」——石头被「扒」成细末，一碰手就「扒」得满身灰；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘）→ pulverizare（使成灰）→ 法语 pulveriser → 英语 pulverise，后缀 -ise 表示「使……化」，核心义「化为尘粉」。注意它与英语 powder 并无共同词根。

sensesIntro.en: Pulverise begins with grinding to dust, moves through physical destruction, and then extends to beating rivals and crushing arguments.
sensesIntro.cn: pulverise 先指研磨成粉，再指物理上的摧毁，随后延伸到击败对手与驳倒论点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone struck until only a layer of dust remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头被敲到只剩薄薄一层灰尘。

branches.en: Grinding to powder is the literal central sense.
branches.cn: 研磨成粉是字面核心义项。

branches.en: Physical destruction extends the grinding image to force.
branches.cn: 物理摧毁把研磨意象扩展到暴力破坏。

branches.en: Beating a rival and attacking an argument both use the dust image figuratively.
branches.cn: 击败对手与抨击论点都是「成尘」画面的比喻用法。

branches.en: The intransitive sense describes the material that crumbles.
branches.cn: 不及物义项侧重那本身碎裂的材料。

branches.en: Both senses share one outcome: the solid becomes fragments.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一结果：固体变成碎屑。

intro.en: Pulverise is the root pulver- plus the verb suffix -ise, with pulverisation and pulveriser built around it.
intro.cn: pulverise 由词根 pulver- 加动词后缀 -ise 构成，周围有 pulverisation 与 pulveriser。

latinIntro.en: Latin pulvis means dust, and pulverizare means to turn something into dust.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pulvis 意为灰尘，pulverizare 意为使某物化为灰尘。

items.example: Pulvis supplies the dust image.
items.exampleCN: pulvis 提供「灰尘」的意象。

items.example: The root pulver- appears in powder words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pulver- 出现在表示粉末的词中。

items.example: Pulverizare is the direct verb source.
items.exampleCN: pulverizare 是直接的动词来源。

items.example: The suffix -ise makes pulverise mean to make dust.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 使 pulverise 表示「使成灰」。

items.example: Pulverise keeps the literal sense.
items.exampleCN: pulverise 保留字面含义。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms pulverisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 pulverisation。

items.example: Pulverisation names the process.
items.exampleCN: pulverisation 指这一过程。

items.example: Pulverous describes dusty surfaces.
items.exampleCN: pulverous 描述覆满灰尘的表面。

items.example: A pulveriser turns lumps into powder.
items.exampleCN: 粉碎机把块状物变成粉末。

definition_en: a very light grey rock full of tiny holes, formed from cooling lava and often used for scrubbing or smoothing
core_image: 一块满是气泡孔的浅灰石头，轻得能浮在水面上
scene: 她拿起那块粗糙的浅灰石头，仔细擦拭脚后跟，皮肤很快变得光滑。She rubbed a rough piece of pumice against the back of her heels, and the skin soon became smooth.
sceneCN: 这里 pumice 是「浮石」（第 1 个义项：多孔轻质、用来蹭磨的火山岩）；句意：她拿起那块粗糙的浅灰石头，仔细擦拭脚后跟，皮肤很快变得光滑。

pos.zh: 浮石；浮岩（火山岩）
用浮石打磨；用浮石擦净
浮石制成的（多见于复合词）

derivatives.zh: pumice + -ous 构成的形容词，义为「浮石质的；多孔轻质的」
pumice + -ite（矿物名词后缀），指细粒火山玻璃质粉末
复合名词，指打磨或去角质用的浮石块

senses.title: The light porous volcanic rock
senses.definition: a light grey rock full of holes, formed when frothy lava cools and traps gas
senses.definitionCN: 由多气泡熔岩冷却时困住气体而形成的浅灰色多孔岩石
senses.example: Pumice floats on water because of its many air holes.
senses.exampleCN: 浮石因为有许多气孔而能浮在水上。
senses.why: The Latin name for this frothy stone is the direct source, so the rock itself is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语对这块多泡石头的称呼是直接来源，所以岩石本身是中心义项。

senses.title: A block used for rubbing skin
senses.definition: a shaped piece of this rock used to rub away hard skin
senses.definitionCN: 切成一定形状的这种石头，用来磨去硬皮
senses.example: Soak your feet first, then use a pumice gently.
senses.exampleCN: 先泡脚，然后轻轻用磨脚石打磨。
senses.why: Because the rock is rough and light, the shaped block for skin care takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种石头粗糙又轻便，切割出来的护肤石块沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: To smooth or clean with the stone
senses.definition: to rub a surface with pumice to make it smooth or clean
senses.definitionCN: 用浮石摩擦表面，使其光滑或洁净
senses.example: The carpenters pumiced the wooden panel before painting.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠在上漆之前用浮石打磨木板。
senses.why: The action of using the rock produces a verb of exactly that action.
senses.whyCN: 使用这种石头的动作直接产生了一个表示该动作的动词。

senses.title: Volcanic fragments in geology
senses.definition: the frothy volcanic material found in layers of ash and debris
senses.definitionCN: 存在于火山灰与碎屑层中的多泡火山物质
senses.example: The geologist mapped a thick layer of pumice near the crater.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家在火山口附近标出了一层厚厚的浮岩。
senses.why: Geological writing uses the rock name for the whole deposit of frothy volcanic material.
senses.whyCN: 地质学写作把岩石名用到整层多泡火山物质的沉积上。

intro.en: Pumice comes from Latin pumex, the name for a sponge-like volcanic stone, through Old French pomice.
intro.cn: pumice 来自拉丁语 pumex（海绵状火山石），经古法语 pomice 进入英语。

items.en: Pumex names a light porous volcanic stone.
items.cn: pumex 指一种轻质多孔的火山石。

items.en: Pomice carries the word into French.
items.cn: pomice 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Pumice appears in English in the 15th century.
items.cn: pumice 于十五世纪见于英语。

items.en: The word's origin is sometimes folk-linked to spuma, foam.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，词源常被俗解为与 spuma（泡沫）有关。

items.en: Modern English adds cosmetic, building, and geological uses.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了美容、建筑与地质方面的用法。

note.en: Pumice is the Roman name of a frothy stone, close to pumice stone and to other volcanic rock words.
note.cn: pumice 是罗马人对多泡石头的称呼，与磨脚石以及其它火山岩词汇相邻。

entries.definition: made of or full of pumice
entries.definitionCN: 浮石质的；多孔轻质的（同根派生形容词）

entries.definition: the plural of pumice
entries.definitionCN: pumice 的复数形式

entries.definition: the rounded knob on a sword handle
entries.definitionCN: 剑柄顶端的圆头（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: rough dark volcanic rock full of holes
entries.definitionCN: 火山渣；多孔而深的火山岩

entries.definition: dark volcanic glass that breaks into sharp edges
entries.definitionCN: 黑曜岩；黑色火山玻璃

entries.definition: a substance used to rub or polish a surface
entries.definitionCN: 磨料；研磨剂

normalIntro.en: Pumice carries the Latin name of a frothy stone, and its meaning grew from the rock to the tool and then to the action.
normalIntro.cn: pumice 承载着拉丁语里「多泡石头」的名字，含义从岩石扩展到工具，再扩展到动作。

normal.en: The adjective pumiceous, with the suffix -ous, means full of this stone.
normal.cn: 加后缀 -ous 的形容词 pumiceous 表示「满含这种石头」的。

normal.en: Pumice stone is the usual compound in cosmetic and cleaning contexts.
normal.cn: pumice stone 是美容和清洁语境里最常用的复合说法。

normal.en: The plural form pumices appears when several blocks or deposits are counted.
normal.cn: 数几块或几处沉积时会用到复数 pumices。

normal.en: Compare scoria: scoria is dark and heavy, pumice is light and pale.
normal.cn: 对比 scoria：火山渣颜色暗、重量大，浮石颜色浅、质量轻。

normal.en: In geology, pumice often sits in layers with ash and volcanic debris.
normal.cn: 在地质描述中，浮岩常与火山灰、碎屑一起成层出现。

abstract.en: Picture a pale stone so full of tiny bubbles that it bobs on the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一块浅色石头布满微小气泡，能漂在海面上。

abstract.en: Picture a bathroom shelf holding a worn grey rubbing stone.
abstract.cn: 想象浴室架子上放着一块磨旧的灰色蹭石。

abstract.en: Picture hands smoothing a wooden panel with a rough stone.
abstract.cn: 想象双手用一块粗石把木板打磨光滑。

examples.en: Pumice is formed when frothy lava cools quickly.
examples.cn: 多泡熔岩迅速冷却时就形成浮石。

examples.en: Farmers often add crushed pumice to loosen heavy soil.
examples.cn: 农民常加入碎浮石来疏松黏重的土壤。

examples.en: She pumiced the rough edges of the model before the final coat.
examples.cn: 她在上最后一层漆之前用浮石打磨了模型的粗糙边缘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡米石」——满是气泡、又像泡过水一样，「泡」得轻能浮起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pumex（海绵状火山石）→ 古法语 pomice → 英语 pumice，核心义「多孔轻质的火山石」。英语中另有形容词 pumiceous 与复合词 pumice stone；与 spuma（泡沫）的联系属于后世俗解，并非可靠词源。

sensesIntro.en: Pumice names the porous rock, then the skin block, then the act of rubbing, and finally the geological deposit.
sensesIntro.cn: pumice 先指多孔火山岩，再指磨脚石，接着指打磨动作，最后指地质上的整层沉积。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale stone full of holes that floats on water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块布满气孔、能浮在水面的浅色石头。

branches.en: The rock itself is the direct source sense.
branches.cn: 岩石本身是直接来源义项。

branches.en: A shaped block of the rock becomes a skin-care tool.
branches.cn: 切割成形的石块成为护肤工具。

branches.en: The act of rubbing with it turns the noun into a verb.
branches.cn: 用它摩擦的动作使名词动词化。

branches.en: Geology uses the same rock name for whole layers of frothy material.
branches.cn: 地质学把同一个岩石名用于整层多泡物质。

branches.en: The tool and the action belong together: the block is what does the smoothing.
branches.cn: 工具与动作相连：正是这块石头带来光滑效果。

intro.en: Pumice is a single borrowed Latin noun, and English extends it with -ous, -ite, and compounds such as pumice stone.
intro.cn: pumice 是整体借入的拉丁语名词，英语用 -ous、-ite 和 pumice stone 这样的复合词加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin pumex names the holey stone, and the related adjective pumiceus describes it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pumex 指多孔石，相关形容词 pumiceus 用来描述它。

items.example: Pumex is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: pumex 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The root pumic- stays visible in English.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pumic- 在英语中仍然可见。

items.example: Pumiceus is the Latin adjective.
items.exampleCN: pumiceus 是拉丁语形容词。

items.example: Pumice keeps the rock sense.
items.exampleCN: pumice 保留岩石含义。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous forms pumiceous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 pumiceous。

items.example: Pumiceous describes porous rock or ash.
items.exampleCN: pumiceous 描述多孔岩石或灰烬。

items.example: The suffix -ite forms pumicite.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ite 构成 pumicite。

items.example: Pumicite is a fine volcanic powder.
items.exampleCN: pumicite 是细小的火山粉末。

items.example: Pumice stone is the common compound.
items.exampleCN: pumice stone 是常用复合词。

definition_zh: 南瓜；南瓜果实；（口语）亲爱的、宝贝；南瓜色的橙黄
definition_en: a large round orange fruit with thick skin and soft flesh, grown on a vine; also used figuratively for an orange colour and as an affectionate term of address
core_image: 田垄上一只巨大的橙色南瓜，藤蔓还连着地面
scene: 秋收后的菜园里，藤叶已经枯黄，一只橙色大南瓜仍稳稳躺在垄沟上。The farmer loaded the huge pumpkin into the back of his truck.
sceneCN: 这里 pumpkin 是「南瓜这种果实」（第 1 个义项：藤上结出的橙色扁圆大果）；句意：农夫把那只大南瓜装上了卡车后厢。

pos.zh: 名词：南瓜；南瓜果实；南瓜色
名词：（口语，爱称）亲爱的、宝贝
形容词：南瓜色的、橙黄色的（多用于复合词）

collocations.zh: 把南瓜刻成灯（万圣节习俗）
南瓜派香料（肉桂、姜、肉豆蔻混合调料）
南瓜田（供采摘或自选南瓜的田地）

derivatives.zh: pumpkin 加 seed 构成复合词，义为「南瓜子；南瓜籽」
pumpkin 加 head 构成复合词，口语指「大脑袋；蠢人」
形容词：南瓜色的，由 pumpkin 加连字符与 -ed 构成

senses.title: The orange gourd fruit
senses.definition: a large round orange vegetable with thick skin and soft flesh, grown on a long trailing vine and eaten cooked
senses.definitionCN: 一种大而圆、橙色、皮厚肉软的蔬菜，长在长而伏地的藤蔓上，煮熟后食用
senses.example: We roasted the pumpkin with salt and olive oil.
senses.exampleCN: 我们用盐和橄榄油烤了那个南瓜。
senses.why: This is the literal core: the word simply names the orange gourd, and every other sense grows from the picture of that heavy fruit lying on the vine.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心义：词直接指那只橙色瓜果，其他义项都从「沉重果实伏在藤上」的画面长出来。

senses.title: The plant that bears it
senses.definition: the vine plant of the gourd family that produces these fruits
senses.definitionCN: 葫芦科中结出这种果实的藤本植物
senses.example: The pumpkin in the corner of the field climbed the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 田角那棵南瓜植株顺着篱笆爬了上去。
senses.why: English habitually lets the name of a crop stand for the plant itself, so the fruit word also names the growing vine.
senses.whyCN: 英语惯于用作物名指称作物植株，所以指果实的词也能指生长中的藤。

senses.title: Carved for Halloween
senses.definition: a pumpkin hollowed out and cut with a face, fitted with a candle or light as a Halloween decoration
senses.definitionCN: 在万圣节挖空并刻出脸部、内装蜡烛或灯光的南瓜装饰
senses.example: The children carved a pumpkin with a crooked smile.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们刻了一只歪嘴笑的南瓜灯。
senses.why: A long folk custom in which turnips were carved and lit passed to pumpkins in North America, so the fruit became the standard lantern.
senses.whyCN: 把根茎类刻空点灯的古老民俗在北美转到南瓜上，这只果实于是成了标准灯罩。

senses.title: Food made from it
senses.definition: a dish or food product made with pumpkin, such as pie, soup, bread or seeds
senses.definitionCN: 用南瓜做的菜肴或食品，如南瓜派、南瓜汤、南瓜面包或南瓜子
senses.example: She brought a warm pumpkin pie to the festival table.
senses.exampleCN: 她带了一只热南瓜派到节日餐桌上。
senses.why: A food word naturally shifts from the ingredient to the finished dish, especially in autumn and festival cooking.
senses.whyCN: 食物词常从原料转到成品菜肴，秋季节令烹饪尤其如此。

senses.title: An orange colour
senses.definition: a warm orange colour resembling that of a ripe pumpkin, usually used before another noun
senses.definitionCN: 类似熟南瓜的暖橙色，通常放在名词前作修饰
senses.example: The sky turned pumpkin orange at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时天空变成南瓜般的橙色。
senses.why: The most striking feature of the fruit is its colour, so the name transfers to that shade in compounds.
senses.whyCN: 果实最醒目的特征是颜色，名称便转移到这种色调上，多构成复合词。

senses.title: A term of endearment
senses.definition: a friendly or affectionate name used when speaking to a person, especially a child
senses.definitionCN: 对人或孩子说话时用的亲昵称呼
senses.example: Come here, pumpkin, and let me see your drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 过来，小宝贝，让我看看你画的画。
senses.why: Round, warm and homely things make pleasant pet names in English, so the fruit became a tender way to address someone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用圆润、温暖、家常的事物作昵称，这只果实便成了亲切的称呼方式。

senses.title: A pompous person
senses.definition: an old-fashioned or literary word for an important, pompous or self-important person
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或文学用语，指摆架子、自命不凡的重要人物
senses.example: The old rival called the mayor some pumpkin of the court.
senses.exampleCN: 那个老对头嘲讽市长像宫廷里摆架子的大人物。
senses.why: Sixteenth-century English used pumpkin with mock grandeur for upstarts, which links the fruit to a swollen, self-important figure.
senses.whyCN: 十六世纪英语用南瓜戏称暴发户，把果实与虚胀自大的形象连在一起。

intro.en: Pumpkin came into English from French pompon, itself from Latin pepo, which the Romans took over from Greek pepon, a large ripened melon.
intro.cn: pumpkin 经法语 pompon 进入英语，其源头是拉丁语 pepo；罗马人又从希腊语 pepon（成熟的大甜瓜）借来这个词。

items.en: Pepon is the word for a large melon ripened by the sun, from peptein, to ripen or cook.
items.cn: pepon 指被太阳晒熟的大甜瓜，词根 peptein 意为「成熟」或「煮」。

items.en: Latin borrows the word as pepo, still naming a large gourd-like fruit.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 pepo，仍指瓜类硕果。

items.en: French forms such as pompon carry the word into the language of the later Middle Ages.
items.cn: 法语中的 pompon 等词形在中世纪末期把这个词带进该语言。

items.en: English records pumpion and pompeon before the modern spelling pumpkin settles.
items.cn: 英语先有 pumpion、pompeon 等写法，之后才稳定为现在的 pumpkin。

items.en: Once American cooks made it a pie for autumn festivals, the fruit and Halloween became inseparable.
items.cn: 美国烹饪把它做成秋天的节日馅饼之后，这种果实便与万圣节难以分开。

note.en: Pumpkin belongs to the gourd vocabulary, where squash, melon and the old-size word pump can be confused with it.
note.cn: pumpkin 属于瓜类词汇，容易与 squash、melon 以及表示「泵」的 pump 混在一起。

entries.definition: a machine that moves liquid or gas
entries.definitionCN: 泵；抽水机（只是拼写与发音相近，词源不同，无共同词根）

entries.definition: showy ceremonial grandeur
entries.definitionCN: 排场；浮华（只是发音相近，词源不同：借自拉丁语 pompa，指仪仗游行）

entries.definition: a gourd fruit with a hard rind
entries.definitionCN: 葫芦科的瓜类（与 pumpkin 同出拉丁语 pepo 的词源来源）

entries.definition: a gourd of the same family, eaten as a vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 葫芦科瓜类中最常用的统称，pumpkin 是其中一种

entries.definition: any of a family of hard-skinned fruits, or a dried one used as a container
entries.definitionCN: 葫芦；瓜类硬皮果实，是比 pumpkin 更宽的统称

entries.definition: a large sweet soft fruit such as a watermelon or cantaloupe
entries.definitionCN: 甜瓜；瓜（与 pumpkin 同出希腊语 pepon，但多指甜味水果）

normalIntro.en: Pumpkin looks like a fat pumpkin-shaped balloon: the round p, the heavy m, and the k sound of a thick skin.
normalIntro.cn: pumpkin 读起来像一只鼓鼓的南瓜气球：圆圆的 p、沉沉的 m，加上厚皮般的 k 音。

normal.en: Pumpkin pie is the standard autumn dessert, so pumpkin often arrives with pie and cinnamon.
normal.cn: 南瓜派是经典的秋季甜点，所以 pumpkin 常与 pie、cinnamon 一起出现。

normal.en: Carve a pumpkin means cutting a face into a fruit for Halloween.
normal.cn: carve a pumpkin 指在万圣节把南瓜刻成人脸灯。

normal.en: Pumpkin seeds are roasted and eaten as a healthy snack.
normal.cn: pumpkin seeds 是烤过当健康零食吃的南瓜子。

normal.en: Pumpkin is a countable noun, so two of them are two pumpkins.
normal.cn: pumpkin 是可数名词，两个就是 two pumpkins。

normal.en: Compare squash: squash is the wider family word, pumpkin is the round orange one.
normal.cn: 对比 squash：squash 是更宽泛的瓜类词，pumpkin 专指圆圆的橙色那种。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy orange globe sitting on the soil with a coiled vine running away from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉甸甸的橙色圆球坐在泥土上，一条盘绕的藤从它身边爬开。

abstract.en: See the same globe lifted onto a stool with a single candle burning inside.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只圆球被放到凳子上，里面燃着一支蜡烛。

abstract.en: Turn the whole picture amber: the fruit becomes a colour before it becomes a word.
abstract.cn: 把整幅画调成琥珀色：果实在变成词之前先变成了一种颜色。

examples.en: She baked a pumpkin cake for the harvest festival.
examples.cn: 她为丰收节烤了一个南瓜蛋糕。

examples.en: Two pumpkins ripened in the shade of the barn wall.
examples.cn: 两只南瓜在谷仓墙的阴影里熟了。

examples.en: The soup was bright pumpkin orange.
examples.cn: 那道汤是明亮的南瓜橙色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「胖普金」——一只胖胖的、金黄色的瓜，就是南瓜。这只是中文谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pepon（晒熟的大甜瓜）→ 拉丁语 pepo（瓜类）→ 法语 pompon、英语 pumpion / pompeon → pumpkyn → 现代英语 pumpkin，核心义「成熟的大瓜」。

sensesIntro.en: Pumpkin starts as the orange gourd itself, spreads to the plant, the carved lantern and the dishes made from it, then loosens into a colour and a pet name.
sensesIntro.cn: pumpkin 先指南瓜这只橙色瓜果，再扩展到植株、刻成灯的南瓜和南瓜做的食物，最后松动为一种颜色和亲昵称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy orange gourd resting on the soil, its vine still coiled beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只沉重的橙色瓜果卧在泥土上，藤蔓还盘在它旁边。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the fruit and the vine that carries it are two faces of the crop.
branches.cn: 田野线：果实与托着它的藤是同一作物的两面。

branches.en: THE LANTERN: carving and lighting turns the fruit into a festival object.
branches.cn: 灯线：刻空点灯把果实变成节令物件。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN: pie, soup and seeds are the fruit in usable form.
branches.cn: 厨房线：南瓜派、南瓜汤和南瓜子是可食用的果实形态。

branches.en: THE COLOUR: the most striking feature of the fruit becomes a shade on its own.
branches.cn: 色彩线：果实最醒目的特征单独成为一种色调。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: roundness and swelling pull the word toward endearment or mock pomposity.
branches.cn: 人物线：圆润与虚胀把词推向亲昵称呼或嘲弄的摆架子。

intro.en: Pumpkin is a borrowed noun, and English mostly builds around it with compounds such as pumpkinseed and pumpkinhead rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: pumpkin 是借入的名词，英语主要在它周围构成 pumpkinseed、pumpkinhead 等复合词，而不是加前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form pepo, from Greek pepon, is the recorded source; the initial pom sound of French is a later reshaping.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 pepo 源自希腊语 pepon，是有记载的来源；法语开头出现的 pom 音是后来的改造。

items.example: Pepon is the oldest recorded stage of the word.
items.exampleCN: pepon 是这个词最早有记载的阶段。

items.example: Latin pepo gave English the plant name pepo, still used in botany.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pepo 给英语留下植物学词 pepo。

items.example: The French reshaping introduced the pom sound.
items.exampleCN: 法语改造带来了 pom 这个音。

items.example: Pumpion is an early English spelling of the word.
items.exampleCN: pumpion 是这个词早期的英语写法。

items.example: Pumpkin is the settled modern form.
items.exampleCN: pumpkin 是最终定型的现代形式。

items.meaningCN: 小……的，或表示熟悉事物的词尾
items.example: The final -kin matches many English nouns though it does not make the pumpkin smaller.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -kin 常见于英语名词，不过它并没有让南瓜变小。

items.meaning: an edible seed of a pumpkin
items.example: Pumpkinseed joins the fruit name to seed.
items.exampleCN: pumpkinseed 把果名与 seed 合在一起。

items.meaning: a slang word for a foolish person
items.example: Pumpkinhead mocks someone as empty-headed.
items.exampleCN: pumpkinhead 嘲弄一个人脑袋空空。

items.meaning: having the orange colour of a pumpkin
items.example: Pumpkin-colored uses the fruit name as a colour.
items.exampleCN: pumpkin-colored 把果名当成颜色使用。

latinEntries.meaning: a large ripened melon or gourd
latinEntries.example: Botany still uses pepo for a hard-skinned fruit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 植物学仍用 pepo 指硬皮果实。

latinEntries.example: The Romance forms all trace back to this word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 罗曼语各形式都可回溯到这个词。

definition_zh: 朋克音乐；朋克亚文化；小阿飞、不良少年；无用之物；（美俚）小混混
definition_en: a fast loud form of rock music with a rebellious image, its followers and style; also a young street tough or, in older use, something worthless
core_image: 街头几个衣领钉满别针、头发竖起、抱着一把破吉他的年轻人
scene: 夜里的地下俱乐部里，三个少年顶着刺猬般的头发，抱着磨花的吉他，台下人群挤在一起。The band played loud punk until the whole room was shaking.
sceneCN: 这里 punk 是「朋克音乐这种风格」（第 1 个义项：快速、响亮、带反叛形象的摇滚）；句意：乐队一直弹着响亮的朋克，直到整个房间都在震动。

pos.zh: 名词：朋克音乐（不可数）
名词：朋克分子、朋克亚文化成员
名词：小阿飞、不良少年；无用之物
形容词：朋克的、朋克风格的

collocations.zh: 朋克摇滚（比 punk 更完整的称法）

derivatives.zh: punk 加 -er 构成，指「朋克乐手；朋克迷」
punk 加 -y 构成，指「有朋克风格的；像朋克的」
punk 与 rock 构成复合名词，指「朋克摇滚」；另 cyberspace 与 punk 在二十世纪后期合成 cyberpunk

senses.title: The music
senses.definition: a fast, loud, raw form of rock music that began in the middle of the nineteen seventies and values energy over polish
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪七十年代中期兴起的一种快速、响亮、粗糙的摇滚乐，重能量而不重精致
senses.example: The band plays fast punk with a three-chord song.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队演奏着三和弦的快速朋克。
senses.why: The young rebels who traded sneering slang for a sound became the name of that sound, so punk now first means the music.
senses.whyCN: 那些用这个俚语自称的年轻反叛者后来成了一种声音的名字，于是 punk 首先指这种音乐。

senses.title: The movement and style
senses.definition: the fashion, attitude and do-it-yourself culture that grew around this music, with spiky hair, safety pins and torn clothes
senses.definitionCN: 围绕这种音乐形成的服饰、态度与自食其力的文化：竖起头发、别针、破旧衣服
senses.example: Her jacket pins and bleached hair are pure punk.
senses.exampleCN: 她外套上的别针加上漂白过的头发，十足的朋克风范。
senses.why: A music scene brings a look and an attitude, and punk covers the whole rebellious subculture rather than only the songs.
senses.whyCN: 音乐场景会带出一整套外观与态度，punk 因此覆盖整个反叛亚文化，而不只是歌。

senses.title: The adjective
senses.definition: describing a style that is deliberately rough, rebellious and stripped down, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 描述刻意粗糙、叛逆、极简的风格，放在名词前作定语
senses.example: They turned the old pub into a punk club.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把旧酒馆改成了朋克俱乐部。
senses.why: Once the noun named a style, English could use it as a modifier, exactly as rock became rock music and punk became punk club.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指一种风格，英语就能把它当修饰语，rock 变成 rock music、punk 变成 punk club 都是同一路径。

senses.title: A young hoodlum
senses.definition: an older or American slang word for a young, unruly lower-class youth or small-time criminal
senses.definitionCN: 旧时或美式俚语，指出身底层、不服管教的年轻混混或小罪犯
senses.example: The older officer still talks about the punks who hung around the dock at night.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老警察还在讲当年夜里在码头附近游荡的小阿飞。
senses.why: This is the oldest modern sense: by the nineteenth century American slang used punk for an unruly tough young fellow, and that meaning fed the music name.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的现代义项：十九世纪美式俚语已用 punk 指不服管教的年轻混混，这个含义喂养了后来的音乐名。

senses.title: Something worthless
senses.definition: an old or informal word for something of little value, useless stuff, or a poor substitute
senses.definitionCN: 旧时或口语说法，指几乎没有价值的东西、无用之物或劣质替代品
senses.example: He called the whole plan punk and walked away.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整个计划称为废物，然后转身走了。
senses.why: The same slang that mocked people also mocked things: worthless material was called punk, and this sense survives mainly in older speech.
senses.whyCN: 贬人的俚语同样用来贬物：无价值的东西被称为 punk，这个义项主要留在旧式口语里。

senses.title: Something burned to catch fire
senses.definition: a historical word for a soft dry material, especially wood rot used as tinder to start a fire
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指一种柔软的干物质，尤指用来引火的朽木
senses.example: In old manuals the kindling is still called punk.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的说明书里，引火料仍被叫作 punk。
senses.why: The earliest English use of the word was for a spongy dry wood used to catch a spark, which links the spelling to the idea of poor or rotten stuff.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的用法指一种多孔干木，用来接住火星；这就把拼写与「劣质、朽坏」的意味连在一起。

senses.title: A genre suffix
senses.definition: a combining element naming a fictional or musical subgenre built on the punk image, such as cyberpunk or steampunk
senses.definitionCN: 用作构词成分，指以朋克形象为基础命名的虚构或音乐流派，如赛博朋克、蒸汽朋克
senses.example: Writers borrowed punk to label stories full of machines and outlaws.
senses.exampleCN: 作家们借 punk 来命名那些充满机器与亡命之徒的故事。
senses.why: From the nineteen eighties, punk became a loose suffix meaning a rebellious, gritty subculture, which is why cyberpunk and steampunk share the ending.
senses.whyCN: 从一九八零年代起，punk 成了表示「反叛、粗粝亚文化」的松散后缀，赛博朋克与蒸汽朋克因此共用这个结尾。

intro.en: Punk is an old English word whose deeper origin is uncertain: it first meant rotten wood, then worthless stuff, then a young tough, and finally the music.
intro.cn: punk 是古老的英语词，更早的来源不确定：最初指朽木，再指废物，然后指年轻混混，最后才指那种音乐。

items.en: Punk first names a spongy dry wood or fungus used as tinder.
items.cn: punk 最初指一种多孔干木或菌类，用来引火。

items.en: The word widens to mean something worthless, and by the nineteenth century American slang uses it for a young hoodlum.
items.cn: 词义扩大到指无用之物，到十九世纪美式俚语用它指年轻混混。

items.en: In prison and street slang punk also labels a passive or submissive figure.
items.cn: 在监狱与街头俚语中，punk 还指被动、顺从的角色。

items.en: New York and London bands adopt punk as the name of raw, fast and rebellious rock.
items.cn: 纽约与伦敦的乐队把 punk 用作粗糙、快速、反叛摇滚的名字。

items.en: The music sense spreads into fashion and fiction, giving cyberpunk, steampunk and many brand names.
items.cn: 音乐义扩散到时尚与小说，派生出 cyberpunk、steampunk 以及众多品牌名。

note.en: Punk is a short, blunt word whose spelling is nowhere near worry, though its rude early meanings are close to trash, thug and hooligan.
note.cn: punk 短促生硬，拼写上并不接近任何词，但早期粗野的含义与 junk、thug、hooligan 相邻。

entries.definition: old or worthless things
entries.definitionCN: 废旧物品；垃圾（只是押韵相近，词源不同：借自中古英语 junke，另有古法语 jonc 表示灯芯草）

entries.definition: arriving at the agreed time
entries.definitionCN: 准时的（与 punk 同出拉丁语 pungere 的「点穿」词根，只是构词不同）

entries.definition: a blow with the closed fist
entries.definitionCN: 用拳头打（只是拼写与发音相近，词源不同：借自古法语 poinçon）

entries.definition: the fuller name of the raw rock style
entries.definitionCN: 朋克摇滚的完整称法，比 punk 更具体

entries.definition: the smoother style that grew out of late punk
entries.definitionCN: 由晚期朋克衍生出的较精致风格「新浪潮」

entries.definition: a rough, dirty style of rock from Seattle
entries.definitionCN: 来自西雅图的粗糙摇滚风格「垃圾摇滚」

normalIntro.en: Punk is one short syllable with a hard k, exactly the kind of sound a three-chord band would shout.
normalIntro.cn: punk 是一个带硬 k 音的短音节，正是三和弦乐队会喊出的那种声音。

normal.en: Punk rock is the fuller name, and punk alone means the same music.
normal.cn: punk rock 是完整称法，只说 punk 也指同一类音乐。

normal.en: A punk band values speed, noise and a rough sound over polish.
normal.cn: punk band 看重速度、噪音与粗糙质感，而不看重精致。

normal.en: Punk came from older slang for a young tough, so rebellion was built in from the start.
normal.cn: punk 来自更早指年轻混混的俚语，所以反叛意味从一开始就带着。

normal.en: Cyberpunk and steampunk show the word used as a suffix for rebellious fictional worlds.
normal.cn: cyberpunk 与 steampunk 显示这个词被当作后缀，指反叛性的虚构世界。

normal.en: Compare hooligan and thug: they are people, while punk is the culture that name came from.
normal.cn: 对比 hooligan 与 thug：它们指人，而 punk 是那个名字所来的文化。

abstract.en: See a single blast of guitar noise hitting a brick wall and rebounding.
abstract.cn: 想象一记吉他噪音撞上砖墙又弹回来。

abstract.en: See the same blast drawn as a jagged line, then worn as a jacket studded with pins.
abstract.cn: 想象同一记噪音被画成锯齿线，然后穿在一件钉满别针的外套上。

abstract.en: See the jacket as an adjective beside a club door: punk, in one rough word.
abstract.cn: 想象那件外套成了门旁的形容词：punk，一个词就够粗粝。

examples.en: His record collection runs from blues to punk.
examples.cn: 他的唱片收藏从蓝调到朋克都有。

examples.en: The band plays a noisy punk style with a trumpet.
examples.cn: 这支乐队用小号演奏一种嘈杂的朋克风格。

examples.en: The older novel described the punks who loitered by the harbour.
examples.cn: 那本旧小说描写了在港口附近游荡的小混混。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘭克」——吉他「嘭」地一响，把规矩全「克」掉，就是朋克。这只是中文谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语古老词 punk：先指引火的朽木，再指无用之物，再指年轻混混（十九世纪美式俚语），二十世纪七十年代才成为摇滚音乐之名；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Punk moves from a rough, worthless material to a rough young person, then to the rough loud music and the culture around it, and finally to a loose suffix for rebellious genres.
sensesIntro.cn: punk 从粗糙无用的材料，转到粗糙的年轻人，再转到粗糙响亮的音乐及其文化，最后成为反叛流派的松散后缀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kid by a brick wall with spiked hair, safety pins and a battered guitar.
core.cn: 核心意象：砖墙边一个少年，头发竖起，别满别针，怀里抱着一把破吉他。

branches.en: THE SCRAP: the oldest sense treats punk as spongy, poor material, then as worthless rubbish.
branches.cn: 废料线：最早的义项把 punk 当作多孔劣木，继而当作无价值的东西。

branches.en: THE STREET: the same scorn is turned on unruly young men and their small crimes.
branches.cn: 街头线：同样的轻蔑转到了不服管教的年轻人及其小过错上。

branches.en: THE SOUND: a raw musical style takes the slang name and also works as a modifier.
branches.cn: 声音线：粗糙的音乐采用了这个俚语名，并且可用作修饰语。

branches.en: THE SCENE: pins, spiky hair and do-it-yourself attitude spread the name to a whole culture.
branches.cn: 场景线：别针、竖发与自食其力的态度把名字扩散到整个文化。

branches.en: THE LABEL: as a suffix the word stamps the same rebellious quality on imaginary genres.
branches.cn: 标签线：作为后缀，这个词把同样的反叛气质盖在虚构流派上。

intro.en: Punk is a home-grown English word, so its word-building entries are mostly compounds and suffixes rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: punk 是土生土长的英语词，所以构词条目以复合词与后缀为主，而不是拉丁语词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin ancestor for this word, so the Latin list only records the recorded Latin verb that produced the look-alike punctual.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语祖形，所以拉丁语部分只收录了产生形近词 punctual 的拉丁语动词。

items.example: The old sense survives only in local speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老义项只留在方言口语中。

items.meaning: having the quality or style of
items.meaningCN: 具有……性质或风格的词尾
items.example: The suffix builds punky from punk.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 由 punk 构成 punky。

items.example: Punky describes hair or a look.
items.exampleCN: punky 描述头发或装扮。

items.example: The suffix builds punker from punk.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 由 punk 构成 punker。

items.example: Punker names the people on stage and in the crowd.
items.exampleCN: punker 指台上台下的人。

items.meaningCN: 朋克摇滚这一摇滚风格
items.example: Punk rock pins the older rock word to the new sound.
items.exampleCN: punk rock 把旧的 rock 一词钉在这种新声音上。

items.example: Cyber- plus punk gives cyberpunk.
items.exampleCN: cyber- 加 punk 得到 cyberpunk。

items.meaning: science fiction with high tech and low life
items.meaningCN: 高科技、低生活的科幻流派
items.example: Cyberpunk uses punk as a suffix for an attitude.
items.exampleCN: cyberpunk 把 punk 当作表示态度的后缀使用。

items.meaningCN: 以蒸汽时代机械为基础的虚构流派
items.example: Steampunk keeps the same suffix with steam.
items.exampleCN: steampunk 用 steam 配同一个后缀。

latinEntries.example: Pungere belongs to punctual, not to punk, which shows the look-alike trap.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pungere 属于 punctual 而不属于 punk，正说明形近易混。

definition_zh: 木偶；布偶；提线玩偶；（比喻）傀儡、受人操纵的人或政权
definition_en: a small figure of a person or animal moved by strings or by a hand, or a person or government that is controlled by others
core_image: 细线拴在木头小人的关节上，手指一动，它就抬手鞠躬
scene: 剧场灯光暗下，幕布后的人十指细线一动，木头小人便向台下深深鞠躬。The old puppet bowed again as the children laughed.
sceneCN: 这里 puppet 是「被线牵动的玩偶」（第 1 个义项：用线或手操纵的人形木偶）；句意：那只老木偶又鞠了一躬，孩子们笑了起来。

pos.zh: 名词：木偶；布偶；提线玩偶
名词：傀儡；受人操纵的人或政权

derivatives.zh: puppet 加名词后缀 -ry 构成，义为「木偶制作与表演艺术」
puppet 与借自法语的 -eer 构成，义为「操纵木偶的人；幕后操纵者」
puppet 加 -like 构成，义为「像木偶一样的、僵硬受控的」

senses.title: A figure moved by an operator
senses.definition: a small model of a person or animal moved by strings, rods or a hand for performance and play
senses.definitionCN: 用线、杆或手操纵来表演或玩耍的人形或兽形小模型
senses.example: The wooden puppet danced across the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 那只木头木偶在舞台上跳舞。
senses.why: This is the literal visual core: a small made figure whose joints answer to someone else, and the rest of the word flows from that image.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的画面核心：关节听命于他人的小人，其余义项都从这幅画面流出。

senses.title: The art of puppetry
senses.definition: the performance tradition or craft in which these figures are used to tell stories
senses.definitionCN: 使用这些小人讲故事的传统表演艺术或工艺
senses.example: Local puppet is still performed at the village fair.
senses.exampleCN: 村集上仍在表演本地木偶戏。
senses.why: A tool naturally lends its name to the art that uses it, so the object word also labels the performance tradition.
senses.whyCN: 工具自然会把名字借给它所用的艺术，于是物件词也标示这门表演传统。

senses.title: A person controlled by another
senses.definition: a person whose actions are really directed by someone else, often without real power
senses.definitionCN: 行动实际由他人支配、往往并无实权的人
senses.example: He felt like a puppet in the hands of the chairman.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己像董事长手中的傀儡。
senses.why: The image of a figure moved by unseen hands transfers directly to a person who only appears to act on his own.
senses.whyCN: 「被看不见的手操纵」的画面直接转到表面自主、实则受人摆布的人身上。

senses.title: A dependent regime
senses.definition: a government that keeps its name and symbols but takes its orders from an outside power
senses.definitionCN: 保留名义与旗帜、实际听命于外部强权的政府
senses.example: After the invasion a puppet was installed in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵之后，一个傀儡政权被扶上了首都。
senses.why: Political language scales the same image up from one person to a whole state, so the hands become a foreign power.
senses.whyCN: 政治语言把同一画面从个人放大到整个国家，操纵的手也变成了外国强权。

senses.title: A term of gentle scorn
senses.definition: an informal word for someone who is powerless, stiff, or easily led, used with mild contempt
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对无力、僵硬或易被牵着走的人略带轻蔑的称呼
senses.example: Stop acting like a puppet and make one choice of your own.
senses.exampleCN: 别再像提线木偶一样，自己做一次决定吧。
senses.why: Everyday speech keeps the wooden stiffness of the figure as gentle mockery, so a person without initiative is called a puppet.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语保留了小人的木头僵硬感作为温和嘲弄，于是没有主见的人被称为木偶。

senses.title: A pet name for something clumsy
senses.definition: a warm name for a clumsy or silly person or creature, closer to affection than insult
senses.definitionCN: 对笨拙或傻气的人或动物的亲切称呼，更多是爱意而非责骂
senses.example: Come here, you silly wooden puppet, and sit by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 过来，你这只傻乎乎的笨木偶，坐到火边来。
senses.why: A made figure that is clumsy but harmless makes an easy pet name, so the word can soften from mockery into tenderness.
senses.whyCN: 一只笨拙却无害的木头人很容易被当作昵称，这个词因此能从嘲弄转为温柔。

senses.title: A puppet-shaped lure
senses.definition: a fishing lure that is roughly shaped and jointed like a small figure, used by anglers
senses.definitionCN: 外形与关节近似小人、供垂钓者使用的鱼饵
senses.example: The shop sells a bright plastic puppet for lake fishing.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店卖一种钓湖鱼用的鲜艳塑料木偶形假饵。
senses.why: This narrow technical sense keeps only the shape and the jointed movement of the figure, which shows how far the picture can travel.
senses.whyCN: 这个狭窄的技术义只保留小人的外形与关节动作，正说明这幅画面可以走多远。

senses.title: The old spelling of poppet
senses.definition: a historical spelling of poppet, meaning a small doll or a term of affection for a child
senses.definitionCN: poppet 的旧式拼写，指小玩偶或对孩子的爱称
senses.example: In old town records a puppet may simply mean a small doll.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的城镇记录里，puppet 可能就只是指一只小玩偶。
senses.why: Puppet and poppet were long the same word spelled two ways, so older texts use puppet for a simple doll or a dear little one.
senses.whyCN: puppet 与 poppet 长期是同一个词的两种写法，所以旧文献用 puppet 指普通玩偶或亲爱的孩子。

intro.en: Puppet comes from Old French poupette, a diminutive of poupe, meaning a doll shaped like a baby; the deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: puppet 来自古法语 poupette，是 poupe 的指小形式，poupe 指做成婴儿模样的玩偶；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin pupa, a girl or doll, is the related form usually suggested for the Romance family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pupa（女孩、玩偶）通常被认为是这个罗曼语词族的关联形式。

items.en: Poupe means a doll and poupette, with its small-making ending, means a little doll.
items.cn: poupe 指玩偶，带指小词尾的 poupette 指小玩偶。

items.en: English takes the French form as popet or poppet, spelling the same word several ways.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式作 popet 或 poppet，同一个词有多种写法。

items.en: By now poppet names a jointed figure moved by wires in street shows and fairs.
items.cn: 到此时，poppet 已指街头与集市上用线操纵的关节小人。

items.en: The figurative sense of a person controlled by others spreads through politics in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 「受他人操纵的人」这一比喻义在十九至二十世纪经政治语境扩散开来。

note.en: Puppet lives among doll words, stage craft words and the verbs marionette and manipulate that describe being moved.
note.cn: puppet 处在玩偶词、舞台工艺词之间，也靠近描述「被牵动」的 marionette 与 manipulate。

entries.definition: a small doll, or an affectionate word for a child
entries.definitionCN: 小玩偶，或对孩子的爱称（与 puppet 同源同词，只是拼写与用法分化）

entries.definition: a young dog
entries.definitionCN: 小狗；幼犬（只是拼写与词源都牵涉法语玩偶词，义项已完全不同，注意别混）

entries.definition: a person who works or controls puppets
entries.definitionCN: 操纵木偶的艺人；也指幕后操纵者

entries.definition: a puppet moved by strings from above
entries.definitionCN: 提线木偶（特指从上方用线操纵的玩偶）

entries.definition: a small model of a human figure for play
entries.definitionCN: 玩偶；洋娃娃（供孩子玩耍，不由人操纵动作）

entries.definition: a person used by others for their own purposes
entries.definitionCN: 被人利用的棋子式人物（与 puppet 的第三义项接近）

normalIntro.en: Puppet sounds like a tiny pop of wood: pup plus the little -et ending, a small doll with joints.
normalIntro.cn: puppet 听起来像木头轻轻一响：pup 加上小小的 -et 词尾，就是一只带关节的小玩偶。

normal.en: Puppet show and hand puppet are the everyday uses, both about a figure in motion.
normal.cn: puppet show 与 hand puppet 是最日常的用法，都关乎被牵动的小人。

normal.en: The -et ending is a small-making suffix borrowed from French, so puppet is literally a little doll.
normal.cn: -et 是借自法语的指小词尾，所以 puppet 字面上就是「小玩偶」。

normal.en: Puppet government and puppet state carry the figure from the stage into politics.
normal.cn: puppet government 与 puppet state 把这只小人从舞台带进政治。

normal.en: The person holding the strings is the puppeteer or puppet master.
normal.cn: 牵着线的人是 puppeteer，也叫 puppet master。

normal.en: Compare poppet and puppet: they were once one word, and the older spelling is still used for a doll.
normal.cn: 对比 poppet 与 puppet：它们原本是同一个词，旧拼写今天仍指玩偶。

abstract.en: Picture five thin strings rising from a wooden figure and vanishing into a dark ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想象五根细线从木头小人身上升起，消失在黑暗的天花板里。

abstract.en: Watch the same strings rise into a pair of hands and see the figure turn the way the hands choose.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的线升进一双手里，看小人按那双手的选择转身。

abstract.en: Move the hands away and picture a person with a blank face doing whatever the hands suggest.
abstract.cn: 把手移开，想象一个面无表情、按手势行动的人。

examples.en: The designer made a cloth puppet with a moving jaw.
examples.cn: 那位设计师做了一只下巴会动的布偶。

examples.en: Critics say the council is a puppet with no real voice.
examples.cn: 批评者说那个委员会不过是没有真正声音的傀儡。

examples.en: Two puppets shared the stage in the afternoon show.
examples.cn: 两只木偶在下午的演出中同台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕皮特」——帕子包着的皮特小木偶，一拉线就动。这只是中文谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 poupe（玩偶；一般认为关联拉丁语 pupa「女孩、洋娃娃」）→ 指小形式 poupette → 英语 popet / poppet / puppet，核心义「被牵着动的小人」，再比喻为受操纵的人。

sensesIntro.en: Puppet starts as a jointed doll on strings, spreads to the art of moving it, then to people and states moved the same way, and finally to softer and narrower uses.
sensesIntro.cn: puppet 先是线上的关节玩偶，再扩展到操纵它的艺术，再转到同样被牵动的人与政权，最后落到更柔和与更狭窄的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden figure with five thin strings lifting from its joints toward a hand above.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木头小人，五根细线从它的关节向上拉住一只举起的手。

branches.en: THE STAGE OBJECT: the jointed figure is the concrete starting point of every other sense.
branches.cn: 舞台物件线：关节小人是其他所有义项的具体起点。

branches.en: THE ART: the figure plus a performer makes puppetry a tradition of its own.
branches.cn: 艺术线：小人加上表演者，使木偶戏成为独立的传统。

branches.en: THE PERSON: strings become invisible orders, and a person without will is called a puppet.
branches.cn: 人物线：线变成了看不见的命令，失去意志的人就被称为傀儡。

branches.en: THE STATE: politics scales the same image up to a government kept in place by others.
branches.cn: 政权线：政治把同一画面放大到由他人维持的政府。

branches.en: THE EDGES: the figure softens into an endearing nickname, narrows into a lure, and returns to its old spelling.
branches.cn: 边缘线：小人软化为昵称，窄化为鱼饵，又回到旧日拼写。

intro.en: Puppet is built on a French diminutive, so the -et ending means small; English then adds -ry, -eer and -like to grow the family.
intro.cn: puppet 建在法语指小形式上，词尾 -et 表示「小」；英语再加 -ry、-eer、-like 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pupa, meaning a girl or a doll, is usually named as the related form; the step from puppa to French poupe is less certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pupa（女孩、玩偶）通常被列为关联形式；从 puppa 到法语 poupe 的演变链则不那么确定。

items.example: Pupa is the usual Latin form linked to the Romance doll words.
items.exampleCN: pupa 是常被联系到罗曼语玩偶词的拉丁语形式。

items.example: Poupette carries a small-making ending from French.
items.exampleCN: poupette 带着法语的指小词尾。

items.example: The suffix -et marks a small version of something.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -et 标出某物的小型版本。

items.meaning: a small doll or a dear child
items.example: Poppet is an older spelling of the same word.
items.exampleCN: poppet 是同一个词较早的写法。

items.meaning: a jointed figure moved by strings
items.example: Puppet keeps the small-doll meaning but adds movement.
items.exampleCN: puppet 保留小玩偶义，又加上了动作。

items.meaningCN: 表示技艺或行业的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ry builds puppetry from puppet.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ry 由 puppet 构成 puppetry。

items.meaning: the art of making and performing with puppets
items.example: Puppetry names the whole craft, not one object.
items.exampleCN: puppetry 指整门手艺，不是某一件东西。

items.example: Puppeteer adds the French person suffix -eer.
items.exampleCN: puppeteer 加上法语的表人后缀 -eer。

items.example: The suffix -like builds puppetlike, meaning stiff and controlled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 puppetlike，意为僵硬受控的。

latinEntries.example: Pupa is generally taken as the related Latin form.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pupa 一般认为是对应的拉丁语关联形式。

definition_zh: 使纯净；净化；提纯；洗涤（心灵、思想）；使（宗教上）洁净
definition_en: to remove dirt, harmful substances, or anything unwanted from something so that it becomes pure
core_image: 浑水经过一层层细砂滤网，滴下来的水变清、变亮
scene: 山泉入口处装了一台小型净水器。A small filter by the spring purifies the water before it reaches the village.
sceneCN: 这里 purify 是「净化」（第 1 个义项：去除杂质使变纯）；句意：山泉旁的一台小净水器先净化泉水，再送到村里。

pos.zh: 使纯净；净化；提纯
变得纯净

derivatives.zh: 由 purify 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「净化；提纯」
由 purify 加施事后缀 -er 构成，指「净化器；净化装置」
与动词 purify 共享拉丁词根 pur-，由 -ity 构成名词，义为「纯净；纯洁」

senses.title: To make something pure
senses.definition: to remove dirt, pollution, or harmful things so that something becomes clean and safe
senses.definitionCN: 去除污物、污染物或有害物质，使某物变得干净、安全
senses.example: The filter purifies the water from the well.
senses.exampleCN: 这个过滤器净化井里打上来的水。
senses.why: The Latin root pur- means pure, and the suffix -ify means to make, so to purify is literally to make pure.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 pur- 意为「纯净」，后缀 -ify 表示「使成为」，所以 purify 字面就是「使变纯」，这是最贴近核心意象的义项。

senses.title: To refine a substance
senses.definition: to separate a substance from the other things mixed with it so that it reaches a high degree of purity
senses.definitionCN: 把某种物质与混杂在一起的其他东西分开，使其达到很高的纯度
senses.example: Workers purify the gold before it is shaped into rings.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们先把黄金提纯，再把它打造成戒指。
senses.why: In chemistry and industry, removing impurities is exactly the same action as making something pure, so the general verb takes on a technical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在化学和工业中「去掉杂质」与「使变纯」是同一个动作，于是这个一般动词自然带上技术含义，指把混合物中的目标物质分离出来。

senses.title: To cleanse the mind or soul
senses.definition: to free the mind, heart, or spirit from guilt, bad thoughts, or other moral impurities
senses.definitionCN: 使思想、内心或精神摆脱罪责、恶念等道德上的杂质
senses.example: A long walk by the sea can purify troubled thoughts.
senses.exampleCN: 沿着海边长时间散步可以净化纷乱的思绪。
senses.why: The physical image of a filter is transferred to the inner world, where bad thoughts are treated like dirt to be removed.
senses.whyCN: 把滤网过滤杂质的具体画面转到内心世界：恶念和负罪感被当作污垢，需要被清除，于是就有了「洗涤心灵」的抽象义。

senses.title: To make something ritually clean
senses.definition: to make a person, place, or object clean according to a religious or ritual rule
senses.definitionCN: 按照宗教或礼仪规定，使某人、某地或某物变得洁净
senses.example: Pilgrims wash their hands to purify themselves before prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者祈祷前洗手以示洁净。
senses.why: Ancient ritual washing used the same word as ordinary cleaning, because in worship being clean and being holy are closely linked.
senses.whyCN: 古代仪式中的洗濯和日常清洗用同一个词，因为在宗教观念里「洁净」与「神圣」紧密相连，所以 purify 也指按规矩完成礼仪上的洁净。

senses.title: To remove something unwanted
senses.definition: to remove people, ideas, or things that are considered undesirable from a group or system
senses.definitionCN: 把被认为不受欢迎的人、观念或事物从组织或体系中清除出去
senses.example: The new leaders tried to purify the party of its old factions.
senses.exampleCN: 新领导层试图清除党内的旧派系。
senses.why: If impurities can be filtered out, then unwanted members can be filtered out too, so the verb extends to social and political cleaning.
senses.whyCN: 既然杂质能被滤掉，不受欢迎的成员也能被滤掉，于是这个词延伸到组织和社会层面，表示「清除、肃清」。

senses.title: To become pure
senses.definition: to become clean or pure without an object, especially in technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 不接宾语时表示自身变得干净或纯净，多用于技术性写作
senses.example: Under sunlight the water slowly purifies.
senses.exampleCN: 在阳光下，水慢慢变得纯净。
senses.why: Since the thing being cleaned can clean itself, the verb gained an intransitive use where the substance is the subject.
senses.whyCN: 被净化的东西也可以自己变干净，于是动词获得不及物用法，把被净化物放到主语位置，句意变成「变纯」。

intro.en: Purify is a French and Latin formation built on the adjective pure, with the suffix that means to make.
intro.cn: purify 是经由法语、拉丁语构成的词，以形容词 pure 为词干，加上表示「使成为」的后缀。

items.en: Purus means clean or unmixed, and purus plus ficare (to make) gives the Late Latin verb purificare.
items.cn: purus 意为干净的、纯粹的；purus 加上 ficare（做、使）构成晚期拉丁动词 purificare。

items.en: Christian writers use purificare for cleansing rites of the church.
items.cn: 基督教作家用 purificare 指教会的洁净仪式。

items.en: Old French purifier carries the verb to France, and it appears in English from around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 purifier 把这个词带到法国，并在十四世纪前后进入英语。

items.en: Middle English purifien is used for cleaning both the body and the soul.
items.cn: 中古英语 purifien 既指洗净身体，也指净化灵魂。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to chemical refining, water filters, and even political cleansing.
items.cn: 现代英语把该词扩展到化学精炼、净水设备，甚至政治清洗。

note.en: Purify shares its root with purity and purifier, and it sits near verbs such as clean, refine, and cleanse.
note.cn: purify 与 purity、purifier 同根，在意义上靠近 clean、refine、cleanse 等动词。

entries.definition: the state of being pure
entries.definitionCN: 纯净；纯洁

entries.definition: a device that removes dirt from air or water
entries.definitionCN: 净化器；净化装置

entries.definition: to decay and give off a bad smell
entries.definitionCN: 腐烂发臭（只是词形相近，词源来自拉丁语 puter「腐烂的」，与 purify 无关）

entries.definition: to remove dirt from a surface or an object
entries.definitionCN: 清洁；擦净

entries.definition: to make a substance purer by removing unwanted parts
entries.definitionCN: 精炼；提纯

entries.definition: to clean something thoroughly, especially the skin or inside of the body
entries.definitionCN: 清除；清洗（尤指皮肤或体内）

normalIntro.en: Purify is pure plus the suffix -ify, so its story is the story of making something pure.
normalIntro.cn: purify 就是 pure 加上后缀 -ify，它的故事就是「使某物变纯」的故事。

normal.en: Break purify into pure and -ify: make pure.
normal.cn: 把 purify 拆成 pure 与 -ify：使变纯。

normal.en: The noun purifier names the machine that purifies water or air.
normal.cn: 名词 purifier 指净化水或空气的机器。

normal.en: The noun purification appears in purification of water and ritual purification.
normal.cn: 名词 purification 出现在净化水质与仪式洁净等表达中。

normal.en: In chemistry, refining and purifying describe the same separation of impurities.
normal.cn: 在化学中，refining 与 purifying 描述的是同样的去杂质过程。

normal.en: Compare clean and purify: clean removes dirt from a surface, purify removes what makes a thing impure.
normal.cn: 对比 clean 与 purify：clean 清除表面的脏物，purify 去除使物体不纯的成分。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of muddy water turning clear as it passes through a white filter.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯浑水穿过白色滤网后变得清亮。

abstract.en: Imagine a goldsmith burning away dull rock until only bright metal remains.
abstract.cn: 想象金匠把暗淡的矿石烧掉，只剩闪亮的金属。

abstract.en: Picture a person washing hands in cold water before stepping into a quiet temple.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走进安静的寺庙前用冷水洗手。

examples.en: These tablets purify the water in just two hours.
examples.cn: 这些药片只需两小时就能净化水。

examples.en: The plant purifies natural gas before it is piped to homes.
examples.cn: 这家工厂先把天然气提纯，再通过管道输送到千家万户。

examples.en: She found that music purified her mind after a stressful week.
examples.cn: 她发现忙碌一周之后音乐能净化她的心灵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「飘而飞」——脏东西「飘」走了、水「飞」清了，就是净化；这是谐音联想，与拉丁词根 purus 无关。

root: 拉丁语 purus（干净的、纯粹的）+ ficare（使、做）→ 晚期拉丁语 purificare（使洁净）→ 古法语 purifier → 英语 purify，核心义「去除杂质、使变纯」。

sensesIntro.en: Purify starts with the physical act of removing dirt, moves to technical refining, and then reaches inward to the mind and outward to social cleansing.
sensesIntro.cn: purify 先从「去除污物的实体动作」出发，转向技术上的提纯，再向内延伸到净化心灵，向外延伸到社会层面的清除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: muddy water passing through a fine white filter and coming out clear.
core.cn: 核心意象：浑水穿过细白的滤网，流出来时已经清澈。

branches.en: The basic sense makes water or air safe to use by removing what is harmful.
branches.cn: 基本义是去除有害物质，使水或空气可以安全使用。

branches.en: In industry the same filtering turns into the technical refining of a substance.
branches.cn: 在工业中，同样的过滤变成对物质的技术性提纯。

branches.en: The inner sense treats bad thoughts and guilt as impurities of the mind.
branches.cn: 内在义把恶念与负罪感看成心灵的杂质。

branches.en: Ritual cleaning borrows the same verb because holiness and cleanliness share one idea.
branches.cn: 礼仪洁净借用同一个动词，因为神圣与洁净在观念上相通。

branches.en: Filtering out unwanted members and becoming pure on its own are the two outermost extensions.
branches.cn: 剔除不受欢迎的成员与自身变纯，是这个词最外围的两条延伸。

intro.en: Purify has a Latin stem purus and the productive English suffix -ify, and it builds purity, purifier, and purification.
intro.cn: purify 由拉丁词干 purus 与英语能产的后缀 -ify 组成，并派生出 purity、purifier 与 purification。

latinIntro.en: Latin purus means clean or unmixed, and facere, which becomes -ficare, means to make.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purus 意为干净的、不混杂的，facere（变成 -ficare）意为「做、使」。

items.example: The pur- root appears in purity and puritan.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pur- 出现在 purity 与 puritan 中。

items.example: Purus gives the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: purus 提供了整个词族的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ify turns an adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 把形容词变成动词。

items.example: Late Latin purificare combines purus and -ficare.
items.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁语 purificare 由 purus 与 -ficare 组成。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms purification.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 purification。

items.meaning: the process of making something pure
items.example: Purification is standard in a water plant.
items.exampleCN: 净化在自来水厂是常规工序。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does an action
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms purifier.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 purifier。

items.example: An air purifier removes dust from a room.
items.exampleCN: 空气净化器去除室内的灰尘。

items.example: Purity tests the quality of the metal.
items.exampleCN: 纯度检验金属的质量。

items.meaning: not pure, mixed with something else
items.example: The in- prefix gives the opposite impure.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成反义词 impure。

definition_zh: 追逐；追捕；追求；从事；消遣；爱好
definition_en: the act of chasing someone or something, or of trying hard to achieve or obtain something
core_image: 一个人紧跟在奔跑的猎物后面，脚步越迈越快
scene: 警察开警车沿河岸追赶一辆冲过关卡的货车。The police were in hot pursuit of a truck that had raced past the checkpoint.
sceneCN: 这里 pursuit 是「追捕」（第 1 个义项：追着某人或某物跑）；句意：警察正在紧追一辆冲过关卡的货车。

pos.zh: 追逐；追捕；追求；从事；消遣

derivatives.zh: 由 pursuit 还原出的动词，去掉名词后缀 -t，义为「追赶；追求」
pursue 加施事后缀 -er，指「追赶者；追求者」
pursue 加名词后缀 -ance，法律文书中表示「施行；进行」

senses.title: The act of chasing
senses.definition: the act of following or chasing a person, animal, or vehicle in order to catch it
senses.definitionCN: 为了抓住某人、某动物或某车辆而跟在后面追赶的行为
senses.example: The police were in hot pursuit of the stolen car.
senses.exampleCN: 警察紧追那辆被盗的汽车。
senses.why: The Latin source meant to follow closely, and the noun first names the concrete act of running after someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源本义是「紧跟其后」，名词最早指的就是跟在后面跑的具体动作，所以这是最核心的义项。

senses.title: Trying to achieve something
senses.definition: the act of trying hard over time to achieve, obtain, or reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为达到、获得或实现某一目标而在长时间内不断努力的行为
senses.example: Her life has been a pursuit of scientific truth.
senses.exampleCN: 她的一生都在追求科学真理。
senses.why: When the object is an abstract aim rather than a running animal, chasing becomes striving, and the chasing image survives inside the abstract verb.
senses.whyCN: 当被追的对象从奔跑的动物变成抽象目标时，「追赶」就变成「为达成目标而持续努力」，但追赶的画面仍留在词里。

senses.title: An occupation or activity
senses.definition: a type of work, study, or spare-time activity that a person spends time on, often rather formal
senses.definitionCN: 一个人投入的工作、学业或业余活动，常带正式色彩
senses.example: Fishing is one of her favourite leisure pursuits.
senses.exampleCN: 钓鱼是她最喜欢的休闲活动之一。
senses.why: Whatever a person keeps pursuing becomes their daily occupation, so the word came to name the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 一个人长期「追着做」的事情就成了他日常从事的活动，于是这个词转而指活动本身，如业务、爱好。

senses.title: A policy of stubbornly doing something
senses.definition: the continuation of a policy, line of action, or course of behaviour that has already started
senses.definitionCN: 把已经开始的政策、行动路线或做法继续下去
senses.example: The minister defended the pursuit of the current policy.
senses.exampleCN: 部长为继续推行现行政策作了辩护。
senses.why: A course of action can be run after just as a runner is, so continuing a policy is described as pursuing it.
senses.whyCN: 行动路线也可以像奔跑的人一样被「追」着走，所以把政策继续执行下去，就用 pursuit 来表示。

senses.title: The chase in sport or law
senses.definition: the physical chase in a sport such as cycling or skiing, or the legal action of seeking a criminal
senses.definitionCN: 自行车、滑雪等运动中的实地追赶，或法律上对犯罪者的追查
senses.example: The hill climb ends with a pursuit stage on the final day.
senses.exampleCN: 这次爬坡赛在最后一天以追逐赛收官。
senses.why: In sport and law, the original chase image is used again in its plain physical form, so the earliest sense returns in specialist settings.
senses.whyCN: 在体育和法律这些专门领域里，「追赶」的画面又回到最初的实物形态，于是最古老的义项以专门术语的形式重新出现。

senses.title: The male courtship of a woman
senses.definition: the old-fashioned or literary sense of trying to win a partner, usually by paying that person close attention
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或文学用法，指通过殷勤关照等方式努力赢得对方的心
senses.example: The novel describes his long pursuit of the young widow.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描写了他对那位年轻寡妇的长期追求。
senses.why: In older usage a suitor chases a person rather than a goal, so the matching verb of chasing is used for courtship.
senses.whyCN: 在旧式用法里，求爱的人追的是一个具体的人而不是目标，所以这个「追逐」动词被用来表示求爱。

intro.en: Pursuit comes from Old French, ultimately from Latin proseqere, which meant to follow closely.
intro.cn: pursuit 来自古法语，最终源于拉丁语 proseqere，本义是「紧跟其后」。

items.en: Proseqere or prosequi means to follow or to pursue, built from pro- (forward) and sequi (to follow).
items.cn: proseqere 或 prosequi 意为跟随、追赶，由 pro-（向前）与 sequi（跟随）组成。

items.en: Old French poursivre or porsivre takes the Latin verb and adds the change that English preserves.
items.cn: 古法语 poursivre 或 porsivre 继承了这个拉丁动词，并产生了英语保留至今的语音变化。

items.en: English borrows the verb as pursue and, within the same century, forms the noun pursuit from the stem.
items.cn: 英语借入动词 pursue，并在同一世纪由该词干构成名词 pursuit。

items.en: Pursuit first names a physical chase at law or in hunting, and later a chase in daily life.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pursuit 先指法律或狩猎中的实体追赶，后来指日常生活中的追赶。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to goals, careers, hobbies, and political policy.
items.cn: 现代英语把该词扩展到目标、职业、爱好与政治政策。

note.en: Pursuit shares its family with pursue and pursuer, and it sits near synonyms such as chase and search.
note.cn: pursuit 与 pursue、pursuer 同族，意义上靠近 chase、search 等词。

normalIntro.en: Pursuit is the noun of pursue with the Latin root meaning to follow closely.
normalIntro.cn: pursuit 是 pursue 的名词形式，源自表示「紧跟」的拉丁词根。

normal.en: The phrase in pursuit of means while chasing or trying to get.
normal.cn: 短语 in pursuit of 表示「在追赶或追求……」。

normal.en: In hot pursuit means chasing someone very closely.
normal.cn: in hot pursuit 表示紧追不舍。

normal.en: The pursuit of happiness appears in the American Declaration of Independence.
normal.cn: the pursuit of happiness 出现在美国独立宣言中。

normal.en: Skiing and reading are leisure pursuits, spoken of as hobbies with a formal tone.
normal.cn: 滑雪与阅读是休闲爱好，用 leisure pursuits 表达时带一点正式意味。

normal.en: Compare chase and pursuit: chase is the act of running, pursuit covers both chasing and striving.
normal.cn: 对比 chase 与 pursuit：chase 强调奔跑追赶的动作，pursuit 同时覆盖追赶与追求。

abstract.en: Picture a hunter close behind a deer that is leaping through tall grass.
abstract.cn: 想象猎人紧跟在一头跃过高草的鹿后面。

abstract.en: Imagine a runner staring at the finishing line far ahead and refusing to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象长跑者盯着远处的终点线，坚决不肯停下。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of hobbies: a fishing rod, a chess set, and a paintbrush.
abstract.cn: 想象一排摆着钓竿、棋具和画笔的爱好架。

examples.en: The pursuit of clean energy is a global priority.
examples.cn: 追求清洁能源是全球的优先事项。

examples.en: Two officers went in pursuit of the escaped prisoner.
examples.cn: 两名警官去追捕逃跑的囚犯。

examples.en: Painting has become his main leisure pursuit.
examples.cn: 绘画已成为他主要的休闲爱好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑索特」——一路「扑」上去又「索」索地追，就是追赶、追求；这是谐音联想，与拉丁词根 sequi 无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ sequi（跟随）→ prosequi/proseqere（紧跟、追赶）→ 古法语 poursivre → 英语动词 pursue 及名词 pursuit，核心义「紧跟其后」。

sensesIntro.en: Pursuit starts as a concrete chase, turns into striving for an aim, then names an activity, a continued policy, a sport or legal chase, and finally courtship.
sensesIntro.cn: pursuit 先从具体的追赶出发，转为对目标的追求，再指一项活动、坚持推行的政策、体育或法律上的追逐，最后回到旧式的求爱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person running hard right behind a fleeing animal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人紧紧跟在逃跑的猎物后面奋力奔跑。

branches.en: The literal chase on foot or by car is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 徒步或开车追赶的实义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: An abstract goal is chased the way a deer is chased.
branches.cn: 抽象目标像被追的人一样被「追」，于是有了追求。

branches.en: Activities a person keeps doing become the pursuits of daily life.
branches.cn: 一个人长期在做的事，就成了日常的「业务」与「爱好」。

branches.en: A policy that is carried forward is pursued like a running track.
branches.cn: 一项持续推进的政策，像一条跑道一样被「追」着走下去。

branches.en: Sport and law revive the plain chase, while old usage applies it to winning a partner.
branches.cn: 体育和法律恢复了纯粹的追逐，旧式用法则把它用在赢得伴侣上。

intro.en: Pursuit is built on the Latin following verb sequi with the prefix pro-, and it relates to pursue and pursuer.
intro.cn: pursuit 以拉丁语表示「跟随」的动词 sequi 加上前缀 pro- 构成，与 pursue、pursuer 相关。

latinIntro.en: Latin pro- means forward, and sequi means to follow, as in sequence and consecutive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pro- 意为向前，sequi 意为跟随，sequence 与 consecutive 也来自这个词根。

items.example: The pro- prefix pushes the action forward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 把动作推向更前方。

items.example: The root sequi appears in sequence.
items.exampleCN: 词根 sequi 出现在 sequence 中。

items.example: The sequ- form appears in consecutive.
items.exampleCN: 变体 sequ- 出现在 consecutive 中。

items.meaning: to chase or try to achieve
items.example: Pursue is the verb of the pair.
items.exampleCN: pursue 是这个词对中的动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动词动作的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -suit forms the noun pursuit.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -suit 构成名词 pursuit。

items.meaning: a person who does an action
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms pursuer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 pursuer。

items.example: Pursuer names the chaser.
items.exampleCN: pursuer 指追赶的人。

items.meaning: the carrying out of a plan
items.example: Pursuance is used in legal writing.
items.exampleCN: pursuance 多用于法律文书。

items.meaning: a set of things in order
items.example: Sequence keeps the following root.
items.exampleCN: sequence 保留了「跟随」词根。

items.example: Consecutive shows the same following idea.
items.exampleCN: consecutive 体现同样的跟随概念。

definition_en: a large snake that kills its prey by squeezing it, or the name of a widely used computer programming language
core_image: 一条又粗又长的巨蛇盘在大树枝上，身子一圈圈缠紧猎物
scene: 雨林里的蟒蛇白天多藏在树上，直到夜里才出来捕食。A python usually stays hidden in the trees during the day and hunts at night.
sceneCN: 这里 python 是「蟒蛇」（第 1 个义项：一种靠缠绕使猎物窒息的大型蛇类）；句意：蟒蛇通常白天藏在树上，夜里才出来捕食。

Python 编程语言

senses.title: A constricting snake
senses.definition: a large snake that has no venom and kills its prey by coiling around it and squeezing
senses.definitionCN: 一种无毒的大型蛇，靠盘绕身体勒紧猎物使其窒息而死
senses.example: The python slowly wrapped itself around the dead goat.
senses.exampleCN: 那条蟒蛇慢慢地把身子缠在死去的山羊身上。
senses.why: The word went through Greek to Latin as the name of a huge serpent, and in modern biology it names the family of snakes that squeeze their prey.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经希腊语进入拉丁语，原意就是「巨蛇」，现代生物学用它命名靠缠绕猎物致死的一类大蛇，因此这是最基础的义项。

senses.title: The genus Python
senses.definition: the scientific name of a genus of large non-venomous snakes found in Africa and southern Asia
senses.definitionCN: 非洲与南亚一类大型无毒蛇的属名，用作科学分类名称
senses.example: The Burmese python belongs to the genus Python.
senses.exampleCN: 缅甸蟒属于蟒属。
senses.why: Biologists needed a formal name for the group, so the old word was taken over unchanged as the Latin scientific genus name.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家需要给这一类群一个正式名称，就直接沿用旧词作为拉丁学名的属名，于是 python 成为一个分类学名词。

senses.title: The Greek monster
senses.titleCN: 希腊神话中的巨蟒皮同
senses.definition: in Greek myth, the huge serpent that guarded Delphi and was killed by the god Apollo
senses.definitionCN: 希腊神话中守护德尔斐的巨蛇，被太阳神阿波罗杀死
senses.example: According to myth, Apollo shot the python with his arrows.
senses.exampleCN: 传说阿波罗用箭射杀了那条巨蟒。
senses.why: The word reached Greek from an earlier name for this mythic serpent, and the story is what first made python mean a giant snake.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从更早的语言进入希腊语时，指的就是神话里的那条巨蛇，正是这个故事让 python 最初有了「巨蛇」的含义。

senses.title: A snake-like head or dragon
senses.definition: a carved or painted dragon-shaped or snake-shaped head used as decoration in old European art
senses.definitionCN: 欧洲旧时用作装饰的蛇形或龙形头部图案
senses.example: A silver python curled around the old shield.
senses.exampleCN: 一面旧盾牌上盘绕着一条银色的蛇形纹饰。
senses.why: Medieval heraldry borrowed the word for any dragon-like figure, extending the giant-snake idea to painted and carved heads.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪纹章学借用这个词泛指各种龙形图案，把「巨蛇」的意象扩展到画出来、刻出来的蛇形头。

senses.title: The Python programming language
senses.definition: a general-purpose programming language known for readable code and wide use in data work and education
senses.definitionCN: 一种通用编程语言，以代码可读性高、广泛用于数据处理和教育著称
senses.example: She wrote the cleaning script in Python.
senses.exampleCN: 她用 Python 写了那个数据清洗脚本。
senses.why: Its creator chose the name as a joke about a comedy group and not about the snake, but the same spelling now carries a modern computing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这门语言的创始人是拿一个喜剧团体的名字开玩笑，并不是指蛇；但同一个拼写如今又多了一层现代计算机含义。

senses.title: A large tropical tree
senses.definition: a tall tree of Madagascar, also called the traveler palm, that stores rainwater in the bases of its leaf stems
senses.definitionCN: 马达加斯加的一种高大树木，又称旅人蕉，叶柄基部能储存雨水
senses.example: Travelers once drank from the python after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 当年旅人会在雨后饮用这种树储下的雨水。
senses.why: A secondary name for this tree was borrowed into English, so the same spelling also names a plant in botany and travel writing.
senses.whyCN: 这种树的另一个名字被借入英语，于是同一拼写在植物学和旅行写作中又指一种植物。

intro.en: Python reached English through Latin and Greek as the name of a giant serpent, and the ultimate origin is not certain.
intro.cn: python 经由拉丁语和希腊语进入英语，原本是巨蛇的名字，其更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: The root is usually reconstructed as something meaning to rot, which is a guess rather than a proven form.
items.cn: 一般认为词根与「腐烂」有关，但这是重构的推测形式，并非已证实的写法。

items.en: Greek Python names the huge serpent of the Delphic myth, but the earlier origin of the name remains uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 Python 是德尔斐神话中巨蛇的名字，但它更早的来源仍不确定。

items.en: Latin Python keeps the same name and first means a huge snake or a dragon.
items.cn: 拉丁语 Python 沿用了这个名字，最初指巨蛇或龙形怪兽。

items.en: English borrows python in the early sixteenth century, chiefly through the language of myth and heraldry.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪初借入 python，主要是通过神话与纹章学的语言。

items.en: Modern zoology makes Python a genus name, while computing gives the word a separate sense after 1989.
items.cn: 现代动物学把 Python 用作属名，计算机领域在 1989 年之后又赋予它一个独立义项。

note.en: Python looks like Greek-derived snake words, and it belongs to the wider field of snakes and reptiles.
note.cn: python 与希腊语来源的蛇类词形近，在意义上属于蛇与爬行动物这一义场。
